 ## Breaking changes
 
-### Editing earlier turns invalidates thinking blocks on every account
-
-The API’s prefix check (see [Keeping the prefix unchanged](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking#prefix-check)) tests whether anything before a Claude Fable 5.2 or Claude Mythos 5.2 thinking block has changed since the model produced it: the `system` prompt, the `tools`, or an earlier message.
-On Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, a request that sends back an invalid thinking block and leaves `prefix_mismatch_behavior` unset gets a 400 error, whatever the account’s age (see [When `prefix_mismatch_behavior` is unset](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking#enforcement)).
-On Claude Fable 5.1, such a request gets the error on accounts created on or after August 31, 2026.
-On the Claude API, Claude Mythos 5.1 already returns it on every account.
-So code on Claude Fable 5.1 that edits its history can run without errors on an older account before the switch and fail after it.
+### Editing earlier turns invalidates thinking blocks
 
-When the check fails, the request returns a 400 error whose message says `The block is bound to a different conversation`.
-To drop the affected blocks and continue instead, send the `thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01` beta header and set `thinking.block_binding.prefix_mismatch_behavior` to `"drop_block"`.
-The response then lists each dropped block in a top-level `input_transformations` array.

+On Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, a request that fails the API’s prefix check gets a [400 error](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors#thinking-block-conversation-mismatch).

+It covers the `system` prompt, the `tools`, and every earlier message (see [What must stay the same, and why](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/preserved-thinking/prefix-checks#prefix-check)).
+The error message says `The block is bound to a different conversation`.
 
 Nothing changes for you if Claude Code, claude.ai, [Claude Managed Agents](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview), or the [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) builds your requests.
